steps.text: Open the door, you lousy scammer!
Open the damn door!
I know you're there! Open this blasted door already!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Good morning, Mr. Haller. You shouldn't be so loud; it'll disturb the others, you know.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: (Grabs Totter by the collar)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Do you take me for a fool, you son of a bitch?!

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: You said you'd have it done by Friday! It's Friday, and all you've done is pack up and get ready to leave!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Patience, my friend. I'll explain afterwards.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Pulls away Haller's hand)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Explain? I don't need a goddamn explanation. I need results, you understand? I need the heads of those bastards on a platter, now.

spans.text: Explain? I don't need a goddamn explanation. I need results, you understand? I need the heads of those bastards on a platter,

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Glances at watch) Just give me a little more time.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: You said five days. I gave you five days. What now?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: The plan is going well. You'll have your results soon enough.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Plan? What have you been doing the past four days?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: You drank coffee on Monday, played poker on Tuesday, went to the market on Wednesday, and slept through Thursday. Now it's Friday, and you haven't even moved your ass one inch from your room.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Glances at watch)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Stop looking at your goddamn watch!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: It’s not time yet.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: What? Are you telling me to calm down?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ...I guess so?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Easy for you to say, you son of a bitch! It wasn't you who lost everything to those bandits!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Oh, believe me, I could tell how little you had left by the amount you were offering.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: ...Yeah, if I had any left over, you'd be worrying about your own head instead of anyone else's.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: My, and here I thought we had a good partnership going.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: (Slumps against the wall)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: I should've died along with my wife... At least then I wouldn't have to deal with this shit.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Would you like some hot water? I can get you a cup.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: You—forget it. Why should I talk to you about it? You don't know how I feel.

spans.text: You—forget it. Why should I talk to
about it? You don't know how I feel.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Not quite... I do know, to an extent.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Then do something. I'm begging you.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Glances at watch)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: (Shakes head) *Sigh*...

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: It's time. Would you like to come with me?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: For what?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Blood for blood, just like you asked.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Here we are. Have you hidden your burdenbeast?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Yes... Wait, why are you the one giving the orders, when I'm the one hiring you?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: My apologies, Mr. Haller. Would you like me to go tie it up again?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: No need. I'd rather you explained why you brought me all the way out here.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Take these.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Binoculars?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Look over there.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: I don't see anything.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Further. There's a convoy coming towards us from the horizon, flying blood-red flags with black skulls on them.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: I see it! It's them! It's them!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Draws crossbow)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: You don't need binoculars?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: But it's so far away.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Shh. Quiet.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Done.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: So quick?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Yeah... Unless there was something else?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I mean, I'm not too keen on desecrating corpses, but if you insist...

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: You... you're sure there are no survivors?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: By the size of the explosion, I would say the odds are slim.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: They're dead. They're all dead. Good.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: You don't sound as happy as I expected.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: I thought I would be, but... it all happened so quick. Almost like it wasn't real.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Now, maybe this isn't the best time to bring this up, but as for the other half...

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: (Tosses out a bag of gold coins)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Take it.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Picks up the bag)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Don't you have anything to say?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ...Thank you for your business?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Those eggheads spent a month trying to track that group down and came up empty-handed. How did you do it?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: How did you know they would show up right here, right now?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Actually...

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Ach, let's talk someplace else. I need a stiff drink.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I wouldn't recommend drinking in your current state.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Ha... what would you know about it?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Apparently, the people in this town drink in the morning to celebrate the sunrise. I ordered two drinks. Which one do you want?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: They're not exactly the same size.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Yeah, the big one's mine.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Why did you ask me to choose, then?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: To be polite.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I'll take the small one then, thank you.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: (Guzzles half the mug)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Argh—burp.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: So can you talk now? How did you do it? You didn't prepare anything the last few days. You just showed up there, pulled back your crossbow, and whoosh—

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: They're gone.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: What the hell was that? Future sight? Did you bribe one of them?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Come on, tell me. I just don't understand. I was sure you were scamming me when I found you last night, but now...

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Let's just say that if you wanted me to lick your boots, I'd get on my knees this instant.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: You're getting a little too excited.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: I've had something to drink.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: It wasn't so hard. It's all about having a good plan, and following it step by step.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Takes out a notebook)

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: You complained that I spent all Monday in a cafe, but the cafe in this town plays an important role.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: It's sort of an information exchange for traders passing through.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: It's where all the news spreads, true or false.

steps.name: Pepper Trader
steps.text: Have you managed to get your spices out? I've tried other routes, but it seemed like they always knew where we were going.

steps.name: Incense Trader
steps.text: Still thinking about what to do. I might just throw my hands up and hire mercenaries to guard the goods. Better than letting it rot in the warehouse.

steps.name: Pepper Trader
steps.text: When is the lord ameer going to do something about this? I can't afford any more losses.

steps.name: Coffee Shop Waiter
steps.text: Hello, what can I get for you?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: A cup of coffee, please.

steps.name: Coffee Shop Waiter
steps.text: Our coffee is strong by most places' standards, so it comes with a plate of honey dates to balance out the bitterness.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Thank you. I like my coffee bitter anyway.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: By the way, could I ask where the town doctor lives?

steps.name: Coffee Shop Waiter
steps.text: The east side of town. Just head east along the fountain. Are you ill?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I have a batch of emergency medical supplies that I thought might come in useful for somebody.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Medicine, not money, is the most powerful currency in the barrenlands. Now that the cat was out of the bag, I had to prove I was worth the trip.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I think my luck's about to change.

steps.name: Jewelry Trader
steps.text: Time to cut your losses, buddy. Your wife isn't gonna like it when she finds out how much you've lost.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Eh, it's just some spare change. I play for the thrill.

steps.name: Timber Trader
steps.text: Ha, that's what we like to hear!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: One more round! Let's go!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I found footprints outside my window Wednesday morning, as expected. Someone tried to cover them up, but it was the work of an amateur.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Have you ever hunted, Mr. Haller?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Wild animals have their own territory, and they follow certain rules when they look for food or wander around in it. Understand their habits, and you'll know where to place your traps.

steps.name: Hawker A
steps.text: Leaving so soon, sir?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Yes, I'm concerned about these bandits I keep hearing about. The sooner I can leave, the better.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Do you know of any other routes out of here?

steps.name: Hawker A
steps.text: To be honest with you, sir, it makes little difference whichever route you pick. They know every move you're about to make, and there's no way to avoid their ambushes.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Have you all been attacked before, then?

steps.name: Trader B
steps.text: My convoy tried leaving by a tiny trail to the east, but the bastards were laying in wait an hour out from town.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: That's terrifying. Has anyone managed to avoid them?

steps.name: Trader B
steps.text: We tried many different routes, big and small, but it makes no difference. You're doomed to run into them no matter what.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I identified where the bandits operated by comparing the convoy routes to the locations where they encountered the outlaws.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I found a few sniping vantage points, from which my crossbow could cover those areas.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: The final step was to lure my prey into the trap.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Hey, kid, wanna make some quick cash?

steps.name: Shrewd Boy
steps.text: What do you want, sir?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I'm leaving town tomorrow. Get me ten days' worth of fresh water and dry rations, and have my burdenbeast fed before sunset. I'll be leaving before dawn.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Here are four gold coins for your trouble. I'll be waiting at the west entrance at 5 a.m. tomorrow.

steps.name: Shrewd Boy
steps.text: Wow! You've got it, sir.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Now get going, and don't disturb me. I need to sleep before the trip.

steps.name: Shrewd Boy
steps.text: No problem, sir. I'll get it done!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Two gold coins would have been a fair price, but I paid him twice that.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: A kid that age can't help but brag when he runs into a stroke of luck. And the more people he tells, the better.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: So you weren't sleeping yesterday?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: No, I slept. Needed to be in top form for what was to come.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: (Takes a gulp)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: So... that's what happened.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: You sound disappointed.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Yeah... I thought I'd hear the breathtaking story of a legendary mercenary, but it ended up being more like one of my wife's business proposals: detailed, but boring.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: A good plan doesn't need twists and turns. The safer it is, the better.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: That's what she said, too! She even had a notebook with her at all times, just like you.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: It's a good habit to have. People shouldn't trust their own memories. So what's she doing now?

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: The bandits cut off her head... I told you that when I first came to you.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ...Oh, right. Sorry.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: It's okay. At least she doesn't have to worry about writing any more business proposals. She'd probably have been a poet, if I hadn't dragged her into my business.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Yes, poet is a good occupation. Safe.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: To be totally frank with you, chatting with you makes me uncomfortable.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I get that a lot. I'm just grateful to those who are satisfied with merely saying so. Plenty more wouldn't leave it at that.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: My brain tells me I should say something comforting, but my heart would never let me.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Sorry.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: (Shakes head) Never mind.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Can I take a look at your notebook?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Your writing is really big.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I have something of an eye problem. I can see things far away perfectly, but things that are up close, not so much.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Looks like you meticulously plan out everything in life.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Yes. Having a plan in place makes things less hectic when trouble comes up.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: (Closes the notebook)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Someone like you must have everything under control, with nothing ever going wrong or deviating from plan.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: I'm sure your life is smooth sailing. You'll never wake up one day only to find you've lost everything.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: (Guzzles the drink)

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Rubs the mug nervously)

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Not exactly...

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Not exactly what?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: No, my life has hardly ever been in my control.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Takes a sip)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Poor thing.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Please don't say that.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: I meant myself.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: (Finishes in a single gulp)

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Alright, I've got to go... Hey, where's my money? Oh, right, I gave you everything I had left.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I'll pick up the tab.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Why don't you take these gold coins? You'll need them.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Nah, I won't. Keep them.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: You're drunk.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: Don't worry about it, I can stand on my own. Farewell, friend.

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: ♪I held her in my arms, before the day was gone♪

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: ♪She smelled of jasmine, beneath the purple veil♪

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: ♪Her soft lips take me away♪

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: ♪To our eternal home far away♪

steps.name: Vengeful Merchant
steps.text: ♪A moment of pain, for a lifetime♪
The drunk merchant staggers towards the rising sun, the great red orb on the horizon swallowing up his silhouette. He does not turn back, as though he is headed for his beloved's burning embrace.
The dry winds of the desert cover his song in a thin layer of sand, to be preserved for the next traveler.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ♪Louisa, Louisa in my heart♪

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ♪Take me home with you, and I'll want nothing more♪

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ♪Louisa, Louisa in my dreams♪

steps.name: Low Male Voice
steps.text: I'm sorry, Totter, but we have to leave you here.

steps.name: Low Male Voice
steps.text: We're headed north, and there's no way you can keep up with that injury.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: You'll just abandon me here?

steps.name: Low Male Voice
steps.text: This is near the Snow Realm. It's a beautiful place.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: But you're still abandoning me here, right?

steps.name: Low Male Voice
steps.text: I'll leave some money for you. There's a village nearby where you can buy necessities.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Stop dodging the question! Answer me!

steps.name: Low Male Voice
steps.text: Totter, I...

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Do you think the same, Ann?

steps.name: Calm Female Voice
steps.text: Don't be like that. You know we can't slow down for you. We have our missions to complete.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: So you're abandoning me.

steps.name: Calm Female Voice
steps.text: You're not a child anymore. Throwing tantrums won't get you anywhere.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: This isn't what we agreed on, Ann.

steps.name: Calm Female Voice
steps.text: No one can predict the future, Totter... We might be back by next spring. Or things may have changed by then. Don't beat yourself up over it.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Ha. So will you come back for me?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ♪Louisa, Louisa in my heart♪

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ♪Take me home with you, and I'll want nothing more♪

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ♪Louisa, Louisa in my dreams♪

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ♪I'll always be there...♪

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ♪...Waiting for you♪

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Finishes in a single gulp)

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: The key. Where's the key?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Is it this one?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: No, not this one.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: This one?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: No... forget it.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Sits down)

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ...What time is it? Must be almost time. I'll wait outside.
The eaves of the roof casts a shadow on the hot sands, shielding Totter from the scorching sun.
Totter could not keep his eyelids open in the warm breeze.
He falls asleep, curled up against the door frame.
Totter! Totter! Wake up!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Hmnuh? ...Whoa! What is it?
I'm here to pick you up. Sorry about the delay; we ran into a sandstorm on the way. Hope we didn't keep you waiting?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Stands up and brushes the dirt off his pants) No, you came just in time.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: But you had fallen asleep.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Just a nap. I had to go out earlier.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Er... why are you smiling?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I'm smiling?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: (Touches the edges of his mouth)

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Strange. Why am I smiling?
